chapter_intro: Jeremiah’s Struggles with God and Judah.

passages.title: Jeremiah’s Struggles with God and Judah.
passages.text: As the nation faces invasion, Jeremiah struggles to serve God faithfully. He is surprised by opposition (11:1–12:17), stunned over feeling betrayed by God (13:1–15:21), renewed by God (16:1–17:18), burdened by opposition (17:19–18:23), and prepared to continue serving (19:1–20:18).

notes.text: Go, buy. The third symbolic act (see 13:1–7; 16:1–9). earthenware flask. A general term for a container. elders of the people. Civic leaders. elders of the priests. Religious leaders.
Potsherd Gate. Uncertain location but likely a dumping ground for broken containers.
Ears . . . will tingle with shock and horror at an account of judgment (see 1 Sam. 3:11; 2 Kings 21:12).
blood of innocents. Likely child sacrifices made to Molech (7:31).
the plans of Judah and Jerusalem. Their proposed solution to the threat Babylon poses (see 18:12).
eat the flesh. Because of the lack of food caused by the siege, the people of Judah will turn to cannibalism (Deut. 28:53; 2 Kings 6:24–29; Lam. 4:10).
break the flask. A symbolic act representing Jerusalem’s defeat.
like Topheth. An overcrowded cemetery. Proper burial is impossible there.
